topicTitle: Measures to promote growth and development

questions.topicTitle: Measures to promote growth and development
questions.stem: Which of the following is a market-orientated strategy named in the specification?
options: Microfinance schemes
Buffer stock schemes
Managed exchange rates
Protectionism
questions.why: The six named market-orientated strategies are trade liberalisation, promoting FDI, removing subsidies, privatisation, floating exchange rates and microfinance.
whyNot: That is interventionist.
That is interventionist.
That is interventionist.

questions.topicTitle: Measures to promote growth and development
questions.stem: Which of the following is an interventionist strategy named in the specification?
options: Promoting joint ventures with TNCs
Trade liberalisation
Privatisation
Floating exchange rates
questions.why: The six named interventionist strategies are human capital development, protectionism, managed exchange rates, infrastructure, joint ventures with TNCs and buffer stocks.
whyNot: That is market-orientated.
That is market-orientated.
That is market-orientated.

questions.topicTitle: Measures to promote growth and development
questions.stem: Which of the following best defines microfinance?
options: The provision of very small loans and other financial services to people without access to conventional banking
Lending by the IMF to governments in crisis
Lending by commercial banks to small firms at market rates
Government grants to small businesses
questions.why: It breaks the credit constraint and reaches women in particular, with strong evidence of effects on children's health and schooling.
whyNot: That is IMF lending.
Microfinance serves those excluded from conventional banking.
Grants are not loans.

questions.topicTitle: Measures to promote growth and development
questions.stem: What is the difference between the World Bank and the IMF?
options: The Bank lends long-term for development projects; the Fund lends short-term for balance of payments crises
The Bank lends short-term; the Fund lends long-term
The Bank lends to firms; the Fund lends to governments
They perform identical functions
questions.why: Both attach conditions, and the IMF's conditionality has been the more heavily criticised.
whyNot: The roles are the other way round.
Both primarily lend to governments.
Their mandates are distinct.

questions.topicTitle: Measures to promote growth and development
questions.stem: Which of the following best defines tied aid?
options: Aid given on condition that it is spent on goods or services from the donor country
Aid that must be repaid with interest
Aid restricted to emergency relief
Aid delivered through NGOs rather than governments
questions.why: It is worth substantially less than its face value, because the donor's goods may not be the cheapest.
whyNot: That would be a loan.
That is humanitarian aid.
That is a delivery channel.

questions.topicTitle: Measures to promote growth and development
questions.stem: What is the standard resolution to the problem of removing a universal subsidy?
options: Replace it with a targeted cash transfer, if the administrative capacity exists
Remove it without any replacement, since the poorest will adjust
Increase the subsidy instead
Replace it with a tariff on the same good
questions.why: Universal subsidies are regressive in absolute terms, since the wealthy consume more fuel, so targeting protects the poorest at far lower cost.
whyNot: Removal has repeatedly triggered unrest, and it raises the price of necessities.
That worsens the fiscal cost.
A tariff would raise the price further.

questions.topicTitle: Measures to promote growth and development
questions.stem: Why is a privatised natural monopoly a concern?
options: It may exploit market power rather than become efficient, and regulatory capacity is often what is lacking
It is prohibited by the World Bank
It always makes losses
It cannot raise any revenue for the government
questions.why: Assets are also frequently sold below value, and services to unprofitable rural areas may be withdrawn.
whyNot: The Bank has often encouraged privatisation.
A monopoly is typically profitable.
Sale proceeds do raise revenue.

questions.topicTitle: Measures to promote growth and development
questions.stem: What does the Lewis dual-sector model describe?
options: Surplus labour moving from low-productivity agriculture to higher-productivity industry
Labour moving from industry back to agriculture as wages rise
The division of an economy into public and private sectors
The split between formal and informal credit markets
questions.why: Because the workers who leave were adding almost nothing, total output rises without agricultural output falling.
whyNot: The model describes movement into industry.
The two sectors are agriculture and industry.
That is financial dualism, a different idea.

questions.topicTitle: Measures to promote growth and development
questions.stem: What is the strongest limitation of the Lewis model?
options: It assumes industry is labour-intensive, whereas modern industry often is not, so it creates far fewer jobs
It assumes agriculture has no surplus labour
It assumes profits are never reinvested
It applies only to developed economies
questions.why: It also assumes industrial profits are reinvested domestically rather than repatriated or lost to capital flight.
whyNot: It assumes there is surplus labour, which is itself questionable at harvest.
It assumes profits are reinvested, which may not happen.
It was developed to describe developing economies.

questions.topicTitle: Measures to promote growth and development
questions.stem: Why do buffer stock schemes usually fail?
options: If the band is set above the long-run average, the agency buys continuously until its funds are exhausted
Commodity prices never vary enough to require them
Producers refuse to sell to them
Storage costs nothing
questions.why: Storage is expensive, commodities perish, and schemes can be undermined by producers outside them. Stabilisation funds have worked better.
whyNot: Commodity prices are highly volatile.
Producers are willing sellers at a guaranteed price.
Storage is a substantial cost.

questions.topicTitle: Measures to promote growth and development
questions.stem: What is the most useful evaluation point on developing tourism?
options: The development benefit depends on how much of each tourist dollar stays in the country
Tourism always creates high-skilled permanent employment
Tourism is unaffected by conditions in other countries
Tourism requires no infrastructure
questions.why: Leakage through imported food and foreign-owned hotels repatriating profit can remove much of the apparent benefit.
whyNot: Work is often seasonal and low paid.
It depends on incomes abroad, exchange rates and security.
It requires transport, power and water.

questions.topicTitle: Measures to promote growth and development
options: Commodity earnings appreciate the currency and make all other exports uncompetitive
A decline in agricultural productivity caused by industrialisation
A fall in commodity prices caused by oversupply
A disease affecting export crops
questions.why: It is part of the resource-curse pattern, alongside the association of resource wealth with corruption and weak institutions.
whyNot: That is structural change.
That is a market effect, not Dutch disease.
The term is economic, not literal.

questions.topicTitle: Measures to promote growth and development
questions.stem: What is the moral hazard objection to debt relief?
options: It may encourage further imprudent borrowing by debtors and lending by creditors
It reduces the recipient's foreign exchange earnings
It is prohibited by the IMF
It has no effect on government revenue
questions.why: Conditionality on transparent use of the freed revenue is the standard resolution.
whyNot: It frees foreign exchange rather than reducing it.
The IMF has participated in relief initiatives.
It frees revenue for other uses.

questions.topicTitle: Measures to promote growth and development
questions.stem: Why is promoting joint ventures with TNCs described as the answer to a criticism of FDI?
options: It forces technology and skills transfer to a local partner and retains more profit domestically
It removes the need for any foreign investment
It guarantees the local partner controls the venture
It eliminates all political risk
questions.why: It may deter some investors, and the local partner may lack capability or the arrangement may become a vehicle for patronage.
whyNot: It is a form of foreign investment.
Control is shared, and the terms vary.
Political risk remains.

questions.topicTitle: Measures to promote growth and development
questions.stem: What is the main criticism of IMF conditionality?
options: Austerity, devaluation and liberalisation required at the point of crisis deepened recessions and hit the poorest hardest
It required countries to raise tariffs
It prevented countries from borrowing at all
It required an immediate move to a fixed exchange rate
questions.why: The criticism is widely accepted, including in later IMF assessments of its own programmes.
whyNot: It generally required liberalisation.
The IMF is the lender of last resort in such situations.
Devaluation and floating were more commonly required.

questions.topicTitle: Measures to promote growth and development
questions.stem: What is the correct synthesis of the market and interventionist approaches?
options: Successful cases were market-orientated in prices and openness and interventionist in education, infrastructure and coordination
The market approach has always succeeded and intervention always failed
Intervention has always succeeded and markets always failed
Neither approach has any effect on development
questions.why: So the question is not market against state but which functions belong to each, and the answer depends on the constraint and on state capacity.
whyNot: Pure market approaches have often produced volatility without structural change.
Intervention without market discipline has produced rent-seeking.
Both have had substantial effects.

questions.topicTitle: Measures to promote growth and development
questions.stem: Which condition determines whether interventionist strategies are viable?
options: Governance: they require a competent, reasonably honest state
The size of the country's population
Whether the country has a floating exchange rate
Whether the country is a WTO member
questions.why: Where that does not exist, market-orientated strategies are safer because they demand less of government. That is the most important conditional judgement in this topic.
whyNot: Population size is not the determinant.
The exchange rate regime is one policy among many.
Membership does not determine state capacity.

questions.topicTitle: Measures to promote growth and development
questions.stem: What is the honest verdict on microfinance?
options: It relieves hardship reliably and transforms economies rarely
It reliably transforms economies
It has no effect on borrowers at all
It is the single most effective development strategy
questions.why: Interest rates are high, it can create over-indebtedness, and most loans fund consumption smoothing or petty trade rather than transformative investment.
whyNot: The evidence for economy-wide transformation is weak.
There is good evidence of effects on children's health and schooling.
Education and infrastructure have stronger claims.

questions.topicTitle: Measures to promote growth and development
questions.stem: Which of the following is a limitation of relying on NGOs?
options: They are small in scale, not democratically accountable, and can substitute for building state capacity
They cannot reach remote communities
They are always more expensive than government provision
They are prohibited in most developing countries
questions.why: Many uncoordinated NGOs also duplicate effort and impose administrative burdens.
whyNot: Reaching communities governments do not is one of their strengths.
They are often more cost-effective on small projects.
They operate widely.
